newsitem.title: USA: NHL-JAGR AND LEMIEUX LEAD PENGUINS PAST BRUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-JAGR AND LEMIEUX LEAD PENGUINS PAST BRUINS.

text.p: Jaromir Jagr recorded his second hat trick of the season and Mario Lemieux had a goal and three assists as the Pittsburgh Penguins beat the Boston Bruins 6-2 Saturday.

Lemieux's 10th goal put the Penguins ahead for good 2-1 just under two minutes into the second period. After taking a pass from Jagr, Lemieux put his own rebound over goaltender Bill Ranford's shoulder from the top of the crease.

"It is my best game this season," Lemieux said. "There were some great plays. It felt pretty good out there. I've been putting a lot of pressure on myself the last couple of weeks. I had a lot of chances to score. Tonight they went in."
Jagr's league-leading 20th goal gave Pittsburgh a 3-1 lead 4:10 into the second. Jagr tallied again to give Pittsburgh a 4-1 advantage just 2:45 later.
Rob DiMaio's goal brought Boston within 4-2 at 7:07 of the second. But Jagr completed his fourth career hat trick with 75 seconds left in the second.
Stu Barnes closed the scoring with 4:43 left in the third.
Ted Donato's goal staked the Bruins to a 1-0 edge 5:45 into the game but Ron Francis tied the score with a power-play marker with 7:58 left in the first.
Adam Oates assisted on both goals for the Bruins.
The line of Lemieux, Jagr and Francis combined for 11 points as the Penguins won their 13th straight at home against the Bruins.

"It's a real pleasure to play with those guys," said Francis. "It makes my job easier. You pass to the left and you pass to the right and you know they are very capable of doing some damage with it. It is the best game Lemieux has played all year."

At Colorado, Joe Sakic's power-play goal with 7:22 to go broke a third-period tie and Patrick Roy made 30 saves as the Avalanche rebounded from their first home loss in nearly six weeks by edging the New Jersey Devils 2-1.

There were 11 seconds left on Bill Guerin's high-sticking penalty when Colorado's Adam Deadmarsh skated down the left wing and drove to the net. Rookie Mike Dunham stopped his stuff attempt, but the rebound caromed to Sakic, who flipped it over the fallen goaltender for his 11th goal.
Valeri Kamensky had the other goal for Colorado, which improved to 12-2-3 in its last 17 games. The Avalanche boosted the league's best home record to 9-2-3.
Steve Thomas scored for New Jersey, which has lost four of its last five games and completed a 1-3 road trip.
In Montreal, Jim Carey recorded his first shutout of the season and blanked the Canadiens for the third time in his career as the Washington Capitals ended the Habs' four-game unbeaten streak, 2-0.
Carey made 27 saves, but was never really tested. The Canadiens have been shut out twice at the new Molson Centre. Carey has both of them.
Dale Hunter scored early in the second period and Peter Bondra added an empty-net goal in the third.

In Ottawa, Rob Brind'Amour and Shjon Podein scored 66 seconds apart late in the second period and Eric Lindros recorded his first point of the season as the Philadelphia Flyers defeated the Senators for the fifth straight time, 4-3.

Lindros, who missed the entire pre-season and the first 23 games of the regular season with a groin injury, had been held pointless in two games. This was Philadelphia's first win with him in the lineup.
At New York, Donald Audette and Dixon Ward each had a goal and an assist and Dominik Hasek made 27 saves as the surging Buffalo Sabres edged the Islanders 3-2 for their third straight win.
Alexei Zhitnik had the other goal for the Sabres, who moved two games above .500 for the first time since the end of the 1994-95 season.

In Dallas, Mike Modano scored twice and Pat Verbeek and Grant Marshall tallied 36 seconds apart during a four-goal second period as the Stars handed the Toronto Maple Leafs their eighth straight road loss, 5-2.
At Los Angeles, Tony Amonte recorded his third career hat trick and Alexei Zhamnov set up all three goals, leading the Chicago Blackhawks to a 5-3 win over the listless Kings.
Amonte has scored 10 of Chicago's last 19 goals and is second in the league behind Jagr with 19 tallies.

At Tampa Bay, Geoff Sanderson scored twice in a three-goal third period and Nelson Emerson and Andrew Cassels each added a goal and two assists as the Hartford Whalers handed the Lightning their fifth straight loss, 6-3.
Jeff O'Neill started the third-period outburst.
In Phoenix, Mike Gartner scored twice in a 3:40 span of the third period to snap a tie and lift the Coyotes past the Calgary Flames, 3-1.
Calgary has dropped three straight on the road.
